entries.content:
**Root cause:** `Fold.glomit` in `glom/reduction.py` was broken in two ways. In standard mode it called the recursive glom as `glom(t, self.subspec, scope)`, but `glom()` no longer accepts a positional scope — the codebase convention is `scope[glom](target, spec, scope)` — so every `Sum`/`Merge`/`Flatten`/`Fold` on an iterable target raised `TypeError: glom() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`. It also had a dead Group-mode branch checking `scope[MODE] is ACC_TREE` (a sentinel that is never a mode), so `Group(Sum())`-style aggregation hit `target_iter` on single items and raised `FoldError`.

**Fix:** Rewrote `Fold.glomit` to (1) handle `GROUP` mode by accumulating each item via `_agg(val, scope[ACC_TREE])`, evaluating a non-`T` subspec in default mode through the existing `Auto` spec (so nested cases like `Group(Flatten(Flatten()))` flatten per item instead of accumulating cumulatively), and (2) in standard mode evaluate the subspec to fetch the fold target (`fold_target = scope[glom](target, self.subspec, scope)`), then iterate it with `target_iter` and `_fold` the raw items — matching the documented semantics that *subspec* is "a spec representing the target to fold" (e.g., `Sum(['num'])`). The `FoldError` message now uses the spec's actual class name (`can only Flatten on iterable targets...`), consistent with the `flatten()` docstring. Verified with the issue's repro, the full test suite (200 passed), module doctests, and extra Group-mode/edge-case checks.
